title: Adding a layer resurrects deleted layers and drops pending reorder/duplicate
description:
Repro: delete a layer, then add any new layer. The deleted layer reappears in the grid.

Root cause: the four add handlers (MainWindow.xaml.cs:4705 AddTextButton_Click, :4734 AddDataButton_Click, :4770 AddImageButton_Click, :4820 AddGraphButton_Click) write the new layer straight to the template on disk via the worker, then call FinalizeAddedLayerAsync (:8738), which calls LoadLayersAsync(true).

LoadLayersAsync clears _dirtyLayers, _pendingLayerMoves, _pendingLayerDuplicates, _pendingLayerDeletes and _pendingDeleteSourceIndexesByEditorId (MainWindow.xaml.cs:2849-2854) and then repopulates Layers from the on-disk template (:2862).

Deletes are deferred until Apply (RemoveSelectedLayersAsync :4489 only queues into _pendingLayerDeletes and removes the row from the in-memory collection at :4560-4561). So the on-disk template still contains every deleted layer. The reload brings them back AND discards the queued delete, so a later Apply will not remove them either. Pending moves and duplicates are destroyed identically.
acceptance_criteria: Delete a layer, add a layer, click Apply -> the deleted layer is gone from disk. Reorder layers, add a layer -> order is preserved. Duplicate a layer, add a layer -> the duplicate survives.
notes: This is the bug the user reported directly. Blocks on the mutation-model unification bead if we fix it structurally rather than by patching the reload.
